COMPANION ANIMALS

Everyday wellbeing for companion animals.

Good companion-animal care starts with an individual preventive plan and careful observation. Product suitability is always a separate veterinary decision.

IN THIS GUIDE

Start with a preventive visitKeep medicine instructions individualMake home care easier to follow
All resources
01

Start with a preventive visit

Age, lifestyle, environment and health history shape the preventive plan. Regular veterinary assessment creates an opportunity to review body condition, nutrition, oral health, vaccination and parasite risk. Changes in activity, appetite or behaviour should be discussed rather than left until the next routine visit.

02

Keep medicine instructions individual

A product suitable for one species or one animal may be unsuitable for another. Never select a medicine solely because it appears in a general animal-health catalogue. Confirm the exact indication, species, formulation and instructions with the veterinarian.

03

Make home care easier to follow

Write down the medicine name and administration plan, keep it in its original container and clarify anything that is unclear before leaving the practice. Report unexpected signs and tell the veterinarian about other products the animal receives.
